description.en-US: Short name, at most 5 characters, unique within the org. It is the prefix of every system-generated location path under this warehouse ('MAIN/Stock'), which is why changing it after the warehouse is in use needs a dedicated operation rather than a plain update.

What the warehouse is for organisationally. It carries no behaviour: a POS warehouse and a central warehouse are configured and moved against identically, and only reporting and selection lists read this.

Parent in the warehouse hierarchy, null for a root warehouse. This is an organisational relationship only. Stock at the parent is NOT stock at the child, and re-parenting never moves inventory or creates a transfer. Which warehouse may supply which is a separate concern, held by inventory_warehouse_supply_relation.
The person responsible for the warehouse. An external reference into IAM with no foreign key, because Inventory does not own the user lifecycle.

How many stops goods make on the way in: direct to Stock, via Input, or via Input then Quality Control. This is policy, not execution. Changing it provisions the locations the new flow needs and nothing else — it creates no move, and a receipt already in progress keeps the flow it was created under.
How many stops goods make on the way out: straight from Stock, via Output, or via Packing then Output. Same policy-not-execution rule as incoming_flow.

Operational state, and deliberately separate from is_archived. 'suspended' means temporarily closed — for repairs, a stock count, an incident — and is reversible by Resume. Archive means withdrawn from the master data used for new work. A resource is usable only when status is 'active' AND is_archived is false; there is no 'archived' status value.
